analysis.summary: The United States, Group D winners with 8 goals scored in three games, host Bosnia and Herzegovina at their near-home Levi's Stadium in the first knockout round. Bosnia qualified as one of the best third-placed teams (W1-D1-L1, 5 goals scored, 6 conceded) and are heavy underdogs, but carry a genuine forward threat through Edin Dzeko and Ermedin Demirovic. USA's main XI is defensively solid and well-organised under Pochettino; their 3-2 loss to Turkey was played with nine rotated starters after Group D was already secured and is not indicative of first-choice quality. This is an elimination match played in front of a vocal home crowd, strongly favouring the hosts.
analysis.home_form: USA topped Group D: beat Paraguay 4-1 (Jun 12, Balogun brace, Pulisic and McKennie instrumental), beat Australia 2-0 (Jun 19), then rotated against Turkey losing 3-2 (Jun 25) with nine starters changed. Across their competitive starting XI, the team averaged over 3 goals per 90 minutes and conceded sparingly. Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie are the attacking spine; Tyler Adams and Tillman anchor midfield. Full-strength lineup expected: Freese; Freeman, Ream, Richards, Robinson; Adams, Tillman; Dest, McKennie, Pulisic; Balogun.
analysis.away_form: Bosnia and Herzegovina posted W1-D1-L1 in Group B: drew Canada 1-1 (Jun 12), lost 4-1 to Switzerland (Jun 18) exposing defensive frailty, and beat Qatar 3-1 (Jun 24) to secure progression as a best third-placed team. Edin Dzeko (40, out of retirement) captains and leads the line alongside Stuttgart striker Ermedin Demirovic and teenager Kerim Alajbegovic. Defence was exposed badly by Switzerland's pressing. Centre-back Tarik Muharemovic returns from suspension, which is a significant boost to their backline.
analysis.h2h: USA lead the all-time head-to-head 2-0-1 in three previous friendlies: USA won 4-3 in Sarajevo (August 2013, Altidore hat-trick), drew 0-0 in Carson (January 2018), and USA won 1-0 in Santa Clara (December 2021). The teams have never met in a competitive fixture before this match.
injuries_news: USA: no confirmed injury or suspension concerns heading into the match; first-choice XI expected to be available.
Bosnia and Herzegovina: centre-back Tarik Muharemovic returns from suspension (key boost to backline); no other confirmed injuries reported.
Edin Dzeko (Bosnia, 40 years old) started all three group games but his influence waned against Switzerland's high press — fitness is unconfirmed for a full 90 minutes at knockout pace.
USA fielded 9 rotated starters vs Turkey (3-2 loss); first-choice defensive unit of Ream, Richards, Robinson has conceded only 1 goal together.
key_factors: Home crowd advantage: Levi's Stadium in the San Francisco Bay Area is effectively USA's backyard, providing a major psychological and atmospheric edge.
Quality gap at key positions: USA's midfield (Adams, Tillman, McKennie) and attack (Pulisic, Balogun) are considerably higher-profile than Bosnia's equivalents.
Bosnia's defensive vulnerability: a 4-1 thrashing by Switzerland revealed fragility under pressure; the Swiss press blueprint is exactly what USA's forward unit will replicate.
Bosnia's counter-threat is real: Demirovic and Alajbegovic have pace and can get in behind, and USA's full-backs (Freeman in particular) push high — Bosnia can create on the break.
Dzeko factor: the 40-year-old captain provides experience and aerial presence but is unlikely to carry Bosnia for 90+ minutes in a knockout game at this intensity.
Knockout context: USA last won a World Cup knockout game in 2002; this is a must-win for national momentum and Pochettino's squad will be fully focused.
USA's Turkey loss context: irrelevant to this game — nine starters rotated when group was already decided; the main XI is the strongest it will be.
